Hi Claire,

Per our call this morning, ZenithHealth asked for a compact CAIQ evidence bundle plus a short sample of runtime query logs to validate retention/redaction claims. We put together the attached CAIQ_answers_v2.xlsx with control-level references and an initial log sample (query_log_sample_20261130.jsonl).

Two asks from you before we transfer:
- Confirm whether Zenith needs logs in raw JSONL or prefers a CSV with redaction annotations.
- Confirm the escrow mechanism: we can either provide a time-limited signed S3 URL and password-protected zip (recommended) or upload to a shared secure Drive folder with restricted access.

Attached: CAIQ_answers_v2.xlsx (annotated answers), query_log_sample_20261130.jsonl (30-min sample), escrow_instructions.txt (proposed steps).

Kimberly

Thanks, Kimberly — received the files. Quick clarifications from our compliance team:

1) Format: JSONL is fine, but we need a small mapping table explaining each top-level field in the sample (timestamp, request_id, model_version, prompt_hash, token_count, response_hash).
2) Redaction: please redact or pseudonymize any PHI (we flagged a couple of tokens in the sample). If you can supply both the redacted sample and a separate mapping that explains what was removed (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED> maps to user.email), that will speed up review.
3) Escrow: preferred route is time-limited S3 link plus a signed delivery confirmation (DocuSign or similar). Our legal team requires validation that objects were not mutated after upload — a sha256 checksum or manifest is acceptable.

Would you be able to provide the mapping table and checksum alongside the redacted sample by Friday, Dec 4?

Best,
Claire

Quick technical note on redaction and manifest generation:

- Redaction approach: for this customer we recommend pseudonymization for any user identifiers (emails, user_ids) using consistent salted hashing (salt stored in our internal vault). This preserves analytic fidelity while removing direct identifiers. We will replace any detected email addresses with <EMAIL_PSEUDO:sha256prefix>.
- PHI scanning: we ran the sample through our regex + ML PHI detector; two lines flagged. Those will be pseudonymized, not removed.
- Manifest: we’ll generate a JSON manifest with per-line SHA256 and a top-level archive SHA256. The manifest filename will be query_log_sample_20261130_preserve_manifest.json. (Note: Claire asked for a CSV mapping; mapping is included as a tab in CAIQ_answers_v2.xlsx.)
- Transport: pre-signed S3 link TTL = 7 days; S3 object ACL = private, upload via server-side encryption AES256; we will provide the SHA256 values and DocuSign receipt.

If Zenith requires full removal rather than pseudonymization we can do that, but it will reduce the usefulness of the sample for behavioral analysis.

-David

--
David Kim
Principal Software Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

- Can you add a single-line note in the DocuSign receipt that the upload was server-side encrypted (SSE-S3) and include the top-level SHA256?

If you can update the manifest and the DocuSign text as above, we are ready to accept the package and kick off the technical review on Dec 9. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
